Points, lines, areas, segments and text

Source: R/layers.R
rr_point.Rd

A layer of a map, one mark for each row of the data. rr_point() draws a circle at each row's position (pings, stations, catches); rr_line() draws rows that are lines (tows, transects, cables); rr_segment() draws a line from each row's start to its end (a tow from shooting to hauling); rr_polygon() draws areas, filled and outlined; rr_text() writes a column's values at the rows' positions (place names, station ids). Each is piped onto a map, rr_map(data) |> rr_point(colour = speed), or given the data first, data |> rr_point(), which starts a map. The data stay in DuckDB and reach the page as vector tiles, so a map of millions of rows stays fast and its colours change in the page.

Usage

rr_point(
  map,
  data = NULL,
  lon = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  colour = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  opacity = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  limits = NULL,
  stretch = NULL,
  legend = TRUE,
  popup = TRUE,
  labels = NULL,
  codes = NULL,
  hover = NULL,
  choose = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  info = NULL,
  section = "Layers",
  visible = TRUE,
  minzoom = NULL,
  maxzoom = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

map

An rr_map(), or the data, which start a map.

data

The rows, if not the map's: a parquet file, folder or glob, a lazy DuckDB table, a data frame or an sf object (points, or lines and areas for rr_line() and rr_polygon(); a table's shapes in a column geometry as DuckDB's GEOMETRY or WKB).

lon, lat

The position's columns, by default lon and lat; for rr_segment() its start.

colour

The marks' colour (an area's outline): a colour ("#c0392b"), or a column written bare (colour = speed), coloured by palette; several columns, c(behaviour, speed), are a choice in the page, the first shown. A column's colours by default: Okabe-Ito for up to eight values, Paired for up to twelve, Glasbey's 32 beyond, the rest grey as "other"; viridis for an ordered factor and for numbers, dates and times. color is the same.

size

A point's diameter, a text's size, in pixels.

opacity

The marks' opacity, 0-1.

palette

The colours for a column, in place of the default: a palette's name (from rr_palettes(), palette.pals() or hcl.pals(), written loosely: "set1" is Set 1), colours, colours named by value (c(Fishing = "#c0392b")), or a function of n (viridisLite::mako).

limits, stretch

For a numeric column: the values the palette's ends stand at (by default its 1st and 99th percentile), and how the colours spread between them, "linear", "log" or "equal" (equal shares of the values).

legend

Whether the layer has a legend.

popup

The columns a click shows, written bare; TRUE, every column; FALSE, no popup. A click shows the row as a table, read from the server (a bundle carries the rows): a column's name, its unit beside it and its description behind it, where the data's dictionary or labels give them.

labels

The columns' names as the popup shows them, in place of the data's: c(speed = "Speed (knots)"). By default a data frame's column attributes (label, units) or a parquet file's own dictionary (an entry of data-dict.tidyverse.org's format in its metadata, as rr_example()'s files hold), else the column's name.

codes

The labels of a coded column's values, shown beside each code: a named list by column, each a named vector (c("6" = "bottom trawl")) or a table of code and label; by default the dictionary's, where it has them.

hover

A column whose value is shown beside the pointer.

choose

For the map's first layer from data: the columns whose values the reader picks, as for rr_map().

name, info

The layer's name in the sidebar and the text behind its ⓘ.

section

The sidebar's box the layer sits in, by its title.

visible

Whether the layer is on when the page opens.

minzoom, maxzoom

The zooms the layer is drawn at.

...

Not used; color is taken for colour.

linewidth

A line's width (an area's outline), in pixels.

lon_end, lat_end

For rr_segment(), the columns of its end.

fill

For rr_polygon(), the areas' colour, as colour is for the other marks.

label

For rr_text(), the column whose values are written, bare.

Value

An rr_map() with the layer added.

See also

rr_map(); rr_layer() for a layer in MapLibre's own terms.

Examples

# \donttest{
m <- rr_example("dansk") |>
  rr_point(colour = c(behaviour, speed), popup = c(vessel_id, time_stamp, speed), minzoom = 9)
format(m)
#> [1] "<rr_map> Map"              "  layers: points (vector)"
rr_map(rr_example("trawlsurveytows")) |> rr_line(name = "Tows") |> format()
#> [1] "<rr_map> Map"            "  layers: tows (vector)"
rr_example("dansk_harbours") |> rr_polygon(fill = "#d9822b", popup = SI_HARB) |> format()
#> [1] "<rr_map> Map"             "  layers: areas (vector)"
# }
